counterfactual_missing_items: No MRI findings in temporal or occipital lobe to support PRES
No explicit mention of seizure semiology beyond hallucinations
decisive_items: epileptiform activity in the right temporo-occipital region
sudden burning pain in the epigastrium
response.rationale: R2 directly matches the EEG epileptiform activity and the hallucination prodrome, which are core to epilepsy. R3 relies on the same EEG but its MRI finding is non-specific vascular punctate lesions, not the typical posterior reversible edema of PRES. R2 better explains the episodic nature and autonomic symptoms.

rejected.why: Gastroparesis is contradicted by unremarkable abdominal exam and normal pancreatic enzymes; no supporting imaging.
NPSLE is contradicted by the established diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis; no lupus-specific findings.
CRPS is implausible for epigastric pain without extremity or sympathetic findings.
Gastritis is only mild on EGD and does not explain hallucinations or EEG abnormalities.
Append-only completion of R4, inherits its insufficiency and adds no diagnostic value.
